faq.Question: Why do only some candidates and some regions have scorecards?
faq.Answer:
Because we are a volunteer-run organisation, we had to prioritise certain regions and roles. Hence, only council candidates (running for a mayoral and/or a councillor position) were contacted to fill out the survey. We prioritised sending the survey to regions where we have volunteers. Therefore, only candidates running for Auckland Council, Napier City Council, Hawke’s Bay Regional Council, Hutt City Council, Wellington City Council, Greater Wellington Regional Council, Porirua City Council, Kāpiti Coast District Council, Christchurch City Council, Environment Canterbury, Dunedin City Council, and Queenstown Lakes District Council were invited to fill out the survey. 
​
Further, scorecards were only made for candidates who filled out the survey we sent them. Only the responses provided in the survey were used to give scores to candidates. For a more comprehensive understanding of candidates’ positions on issues, we recommend you do further research on policy.nz, Vote for Te Tiriti and beyond.

faq.Question: Who conducted the survey in different regions?
faq.Answer:
Generation Zero conducted the surveys for Auckland Council, Napier City Council, Hawke’s Bay Regional Council, Hutt City Council, Wellington City Council, Greater Wellington Regional Council, Porirua City Council, Kāpiti Coast District Council, Christchurch City Council, Environment Canterbury, Dunedin City Council, and Queenstown Lakes District Council 
Ngā Haumi conducted the surveys for Hamilton City Council, Waipaa District Council, Waikato District Council, and Waikato Regional Council.
​

faq.Question: What was the grading process?
faq.Answer:
All the grading for these scorecards was done manually by Generation Zero volunteers. Only information provided in the survey was considered in the grading process. Questions that were left unanswered resulted in a lower grade. Written comments at the end of each section were considered when scoring candidates. 
​
Survey answers on the transport, housing, equity and decision-making, economic justice, environment, and Te Tiriti sections were weighted equally to contribute to the overall score. Sections where the candidate gave no answers were a “-” for the section, which is equivalent to an “F” for the overall score. If the average of the six (6) section scores resulted in a grade lower than “D”, the overall score given was an “F”.

faq.Question: The score breakdown doesn’t seem to match the overall score, why?
faq.Answer: Our weighting favoured A+ grades, and penalised failing grades (D and F). If someone was right on the border of a grade in their overall score, their position on divestment from and/or sanctions on Israel was considered.

faq.Question: Will you release candidate survey answers?
faq.Answer: No, we will not be releasing candidate survey answers in full.

faq.Question: What do the symbols mean?
faq.Answer:
The “?” symbol indicates that the candidate was invited to fill out the survey but did not fill it out. 
The “*” symbol indicates that the candidate filled out the survey after the first scorecard launch. 
The “**” symbol indicates that the candidate was invited to fill out the survey but sent us a message refusing to fill it out.
The “party/group affiliation” symbol indicates that the candidate has a party, slogan, or tag after their name in official electoral data. 
The “†“ symbol indicates that the candidate was elected unopposed.
